# Metrics matrix: how we compare against published numbers

**Generated by `make benchmarks`. Do not edit by hand.**

Every figure below is computed from the result files in this directory, which the same
command writes. Nothing on this page is typed in.

## Read the null column first

On an imbalanced corpus a respectable-looking F1 can be barely better than a policy that
flags every single row. `trivial null` is what flagging everything scores on exactly
these rows; `margin` is what our detector adds. A large F1 with a small margin is a
statement about the base rate, not about detection.

| Benchmark | Metric | Ours | Trivial null | Margin | Published band | In band |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|:--:|
| ToxicChat (OpenAI moderation as Tier 1) | AUPRC | **0.5967** | 0.0712 | +0.5255 | 0.532 - 0.664 | yes |
| Aegis 1.0 (defensive) | AUPRC | **0.8114** | 0.6606 | +0.1508 | 0.860 - 0.941 | no |
| BeaverTails (natural, 55.8% harm) | F1 | **0.7473** | 0.7160 | +0.0313 | 0.364 - 0.839 | yes |
| BeaverTails (prevalence-corrected, 7% harm) | F1 | **0.1646** | 0.1385 | +0.0261 | 0.364 - 0.839 | no |
| RAGTruth | F1 | **0.6009** | 0.5177 | +0.0832 | 0.520 - 0.792 | yes |
| OR-Bench | AUC | **0.7837** | 0.5000 | +0.2837 | -- | -- |

### What each row does not say

- **ToxicChat (OpenAI moderation as Tier 1)** — The Tier 1 signal is OpenAI's, not ours. We supply calibration, the floor and the allocator around it; with our lexical Tier 1 this corpus scores far lower.
- **Aegis 1.0 (defensive)** — Below the published band -- a failed endpoint. Fitted bag-of-words Tier 1.
- **BeaverTails (natural, 55.8% harm)** — At this base rate the margin over flagging everything is the only real signal.
- **BeaverTails (prevalence-corrected, 7% harm)** — The deployment-realistic prevalence, and far harder than the natural rate.
- **RAGTruth** — Threshold chosen on calibration and applied unchanged. Fitted grounding Tier 1.
- **OR-Bench** — Over-refusal benchmark; the operating point matters more than the AUC.

## Which Tier 1 produced each number

Several of these use a detector fitted on the benchmark rather than the shipped lexical
rules, and that is stated per row because it changes what the number means. The shipped
Tier 0 and Tier 1 are lexical stubs written against our own corpus. `fitted_bayes_bow`
and `fitted_grounding` are **evaluation adapters**: they are fitted on the calibration
fold of the corpus under test and are not wired into the serving path.

| Result | Tier 1 in use |
|---|---|
| aegis / defensive__fitted | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| aegis / defensive__lexical | `lexical_stub` |
| aegis / defensive__text_disjoint__fitted | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| aegis / defensive__text_disjoint__lexical | `lexical_stub` |
| aegis / permissive__fitted | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| aegis / permissive__lexical | `lexical_stub` |
| aegis / permissive__text_disjoint__fitted | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| aegis / permissive__text_disjoint__lexical | `lexical_stub` |
| beavertails / corrected_07 | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| beavertails / natural | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| orbench / fitted | `fitted_bayes_bow` |
| orbench / lexical | `lexical_stub` |
| ragtruth / context_withheld | `lexical_stub` |
| ragtruth / with_context | `fitted_grounding` |

A **degenerate** operating point flags every row or none, so its F1 describes the corpus
rather than the detector.

| beavertails / natural (support-assistant) | 0 | 0.0000 | yes | yes |
| orbench / fitted (support-assistant) | 0 | 0.0000 | yes | yes |
| orbench / lexical (support-assistant) | 0 | 0.0000 | yes | yes |
| ragtruth / context_withheld (support-assistant) | 0 | 0.0000 | yes | yes |
| ragtruth / with_context (support-assistant) | 525 | 0.0933 | yes | no |

A **vacuous** bound is one where the floor forced a check on every row: nothing was
released unchecked, so the guarantee is satisfied by construction and carries no
information. The floor is informative only when alpha exceeds the corpus harm base rate.

## Reproducing this

```bash
make benchmarks    # writes every JSON in this directory, and this file
```

The first run downloads each corpus into `data/external/` at the revision pinned in
`controlplane/corpora/*.py` and verifies its SHA-256 before use. `make demo` never
touches the network.
